purpose: Progressive-disclosure manifest for one governed Freedom 250 research package.
title: Nanotubes help batteries, but the U.S. lacks a full home supply chain
question: Where do carbon nanotubes add battery-performance and sovereignty value, and what domestic production chain is publicly proven at scale?
bluf: A tiny amount of carbon nanotubes can make battery electrodes work better, especially silicon anodes and thick electrodes. But the U.S. has only pieces of a supply chain, not a proven mass-scale chain from domestic nanotube production to finished cells.
use_note: Evidence through August 23 supports CNT as a low-dose conductive or mechanical additive and selected cell/formulation evidence. It does not prove a new battery chemistry, commercial qualification from lab results or a mass-scale end-to-end U.S. chain.

A failure to retrieve public_full_text is an access or crawler problem, not a private-by-design signal.
For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
